name: Uriel
overview: Uriel was a male Levite known as the son of Tahath and served as a chief of the sons of Kohath. As a Kohathite, he belonged to the tribe of Levi, which was set apart for priestly and temple duties. His leadership role among the Kohathites highlights his significance within the Levitical lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Uriel means 'G-d [El] is [my] flame, light,' reflecting a divine association with illumination and guidance. Another name connected to this lineage is Zephaniah, meaning 'y-h-v-h has hidden [to shelter]' or 'y-h-v-h has hidden [as a treasure],' though this name is separate from Uriel himself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Uriel as the son of Tahath and infers Uzziah as his father. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text concerning Uriel.
scriptureSignificance: Uriel's role as a chief of the sons of Kohath places him in a key position within the Levitical order, responsible for important duties related to the tabernacle and worship. His lineage as a Kohathite and leadership status underscore his contribution to the organization and service of God's people during the time recorded in 1 Chronicles. This reflects the continued faithfulness of the Levites in their God-ordained roles.
